query: What visit-note signals suggest high urgency?

per_column.name: symptom_severity
per_column.rationale: Clinical severity extracted from the note is distinct from urgency and plausibly carries strong predictive signal about it without restating it.

per_column.name: onset_acuity
per_column.rationale: How fast symptoms developed (sudden/acute vs chronic) is a legitimate note-derived predictor of urgency, not a restatement of it.

per_column.name: presentation_type
per_column.rationale: Type of presentation (acute illness, trauma, wellness) is a separate clinical categorization that plausibly correlates with urgency.

per_column.name: organ_system_involved
per_column.rationale: The organ system affected is orthogonal to urgency itself and can modulate risk/urgency signal; a valid predictor.

per_column.name: visit_purpose
per_column.rationale: Values like 'urgent_sick_visit' and 'emergency_evaluation' essentially encode the urgency of the visit, largely restating the focus variable rather than predicting it.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_urgency
per_column.rationale: Categories explicitly graded as urgent/emergent workup are downstream, urgency-labeled decisions determined by the outcome, constituting leakage/restatement of urgency.

judge.rationale: Four columns (symptom_severity, onset_acuity, presentation_type, organ_system_involved) are genuine note-derived predictors that lie outside the focus and add real predictive leverage about urgency. Two columns (visit_purpose, diagnostic_workup_urgency) embed the word/concept 'urgent/emergent' and effectively restate or leak the urgency outcome. As a set the predictors provide substantial legitimate signal, but the leaking columns inflate apparent utility and must be discounted.
